Lease liabilities A$142.6m EXCLUDED (lease treatment B). Cross-check: on the same definition the company reported net cash A$241.4m at 31-Dec-2025 = 371.575 - 130.150, which ties exactly.

The forward build starts from FY2026 revenue (A$2,027m) and component margins, not from this figure.

inputs.fy0_basis: FY2026 (year to 30-Jun-2026) revenue A$2,027m per the FY2026 results release (31-Aug-2026), not yet in Metrics.csv. FY2026 statutory EBIT ~ -A$125.2m / NPAT ~ -A$53.6m after a non-cash onerous-contract provision on the T-ATS, OPC, T-AGOS, AFDM and LCU programs at Austal USA.
inputs.lease_treatment: B -- leases as operating cost: lease_cost_pct 1.0% of revenue (FY2025 principal A$11.8m + estimated lease interest ~A$7m on A$136m of liabilities at the ~5% IBR, ~1.05% of revenue) charged inside owner EBITDA; lease liabilities excluded from net debt; da_pct 3.5% is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2025: 73.131 total - 13.073 ROU = 60.1 = 3.3% of revenue, lifted to 3.5% for the new US facilities).
inputs.wacc_rationale: 10.0% for AUD flows: 10y ACGB ~4.3% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.1 = ~10.4% cost of equity; ~7% pre-tax debt (SOFR/BBSY + margin) at ~7% weight. Risk is charged ONCE, in the flows and the weights (bear at 25%), not via a WACC premium; WACC is identical across scenarios.
inputs.capex_basis: capex_pct_path is NET of government infrastructure grant receipts (FY2025 gross A$194.9m less A$46.0m grants; FY2022-FY2025 grants averaged A$28m/yr). The US$1.2bn Mobile expansion (FA2, MMF3, steel panel line, San Diego dry dock) keeps net capex at 11%/8.5% of revenue in FY2027/FY2028 before fading to a 3.75% maintenance level (D&A ex-ROU 3.5%).
inputs.onerous_contract_treatment: The FY2026 provision is non-cash when booked but IS cash as the T-ATS/OPC/T-AGOS/AFDM/LCU hulls are built. Base ebitda_margin_path is therefore stated net of an estimated cash unwind of ~3.5pp/2.5pp/1.0pp of revenue in FY2027-FY2029 (underlying 9.0/9.25/9.5%); bear ~4.5/3.5/1.5pp on a lower 8% underlying (further overruns); bull ~2.5/1.5/0.5pp on 10-11% underlying (REA recoveries). Folding it into the margin keeps the component engine exact.
inputs.working_capital_basis: Milestone-billed shipbuilder with A$875m of progress payments received in advance (31-Dec-2025) against contract assets; growth in the order book generates advance cash. wc_capture 5% of the revenue change in base, 0% bear, 8% bull -- deliberately modest given the H1 FY2026 unwind.
inputs.nci: None -- equity is 100% attributable to owners of the parent.
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods routing table: operating company, non-US / cyclical industrial) with section-7 adaptations -- AUD WACC, lease treatment B, interest income stripped (net cash A$182m > 1x the mid-cycle FCF base), SBC kept explicit at 0.15%. This is Austal's first valuation in the folder; no prior model to reconcile against.

TAKEOVER OVERLAY: the routing table's 'live takeover' row applies partially. The Hanwha (US$1.05-1.20bn EV) and Wildcat (US$1.25-1.35bn EV) proposals are non-binding and for Austal USA only, so the listed entity persists and the three standalone scenarios remain the frame. The deal is expressed (i) in the bull scenario's 18x terminal cap, which is the strategic-buyer exit multiple the bids evidence (~11-12x FY2025 Austal USA EBITDA), (ii) in the 30% bull weight (~probability a sale completes near the indicative range), and (iii) explicitly in takeover_analysis, which sums the parts under deal-completes and reports a deal_adjusted_iv. probability_weighted.weighted_iv remains the standalone three-scenario figure so it ties to the component engine.

MARKET CAP CHECK: at A$4.54 x 422.05m = A$1,916m (US$1.37bn). The Analysis JSON's '~A$1.1bn market cap' is stale -- the stock is up ~36% from its 52-week low. Group EV of ~A$1.73bn sits INSIDE the A$1.47-1.89bn bid range for Austal USA alone, i.e. the market is currently ascribing roughly nothing to Australasia and nothing to deal failure.

FY2026 ANNUAL REPORT NOT YET EXTRACTED: revenue, cash and the P&L loss are from the 31-Aug-2026 results release via the qualitative analyst. Refresh borrowings, lease liabilities, diluted shares, the onerous-contract provision balance and segment EBITDA when the FY2026 filing is in the pipeline.

Price A$4.54 is the 21-Sep-2026 regular ASX close (06:10Z), volume 957k -- live, not a frozen print. The stock moved +8.9% over the prior four sessions on the Wildcat approach; the anchor is volatile around deal headlines.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: order-book-anchored forward revenue growth (base-case FY2027-FY2031 average). Equity CAGR is inflated by the A$215m March-2025 placement (ex-raise 3yr 5.7%); owner-FCF CAGR is undefined because FY2022-FY2024 owner FCF was negative.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 12.3% (5.7% ex-raise) vs revenue 8.4% vs EPS 2.4%: divergence >30%. Book value grew on retained earnings plus a capital raise while EPS stagnated and owner FCF was negative for three of the last six years -- the historical series describes a business in a capex and program-transition cycle, not a compounder.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are on the reported-FCF-less-SBC-less-interest-less-lease-principal series shown in owner_fcf_history. FY2019-FY2020 owner FCF margins (6.3%, 6.6%) were achieved at 1-2% capex and near-zero cash tax on the mature LCS/EPF programs; the base case's mature 3.3% owner-FCF margin at 27% cash tax and 3.75% capex is deliberately below that peak.

scenario_narratives.bear: Deal breaks and the estimation problem is structural. Both Austal USA proposals lapse or are blocked (CFIUS/political preference for domestic ownership, or Hanwha's FIRB conditions); the T-ATS/OPC/T-AGOS/AFDM/LCU programs generate a further round of overruns beyond the FY2026 provision (a repeat of 2016->2024), REAs recover little, and the steel transition keeps USA Shipbuilding at breakeven. Australasia's SSA pipeline still grows but only offsets a shrinking US book, so group revenue rises 2-4%/yr. Net capex stays at 12%/9% of revenue for two years because the Mobile facilities are contractually committed, burning most of the A$182m net cash. Mature cash EBITDA margin 7.5%, 10x terminal cap. Nothing in this path breaks solvency, but equity value collapses to the residual net cash plus a thin 1.6% FCF margin.
scenario_narratives.base: Standalone mid-cycle, deal uncertain. FY2027 returns to statutory profitability as guided, but ~A$70m/A$60m/A$25m of the onerous-contract provision is paid out in cash over FY2027-FY2029 as the hulls are built, so cash EBITDA margins are 5.5%/6.75%/8.5% before settling at 9.5% (history: FY2019-FY2025 average 8.5%, peak 11.6%). Revenue grows 8%/8%/7% on the A$1.03bn LC-M award, OPC, T-AGOS and submarine modules, decelerating to 2.5%. The US$1.2bn Mobile expansion holds net capex at 11%/8.5% before fading to 3.75%. Cash tax ramps 10%->27% as FY2026 losses are utilised. Owner FCF is negative in FY2027-FY2028 and reaches a 3.3% mature margin; the 13x cap binds the terminal value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Execution fixed, Australia doubles, and a strategic buyer sets the exit multiple. REAs recover a meaningful share of the FY2026 charge (unwind only 2.5/1.5/0.5pp), steel programs stabilise, Support grows as a share of mix and Australasia shipbuilding doubles by FY2031 per guidance, lifting cash EBITDA to 11.5%. Revenue compounds 12%/12%/10%/9%/8% off the A$16.5bn order book. Capex fades faster (3.5% maintenance) because the Navy and Commonwealth co-fund facilities. The 18x terminal cap is the strategic-buyer multiple evidenced by the Hanwha/Wildcat bids (~11-12x FY2025 Austal USA EBITDA); Gordon at 3% still binds below it. This is the scenario in which the market's current price is roughly fair on a standalone basis.

bear.terminal_pct_note: EV is negative (cumulative FY2027-FY2029 burn exceeds PV of later FCF plus terminal value); ratio not meaningful

entry_price.method: 15% IRR: PV of 10 interim owner FCFs at 15% + terminal value REBUILT at 15% (min(Gordon@15%, cap x FCF10)) discounted at 15%, plus net cash, per diluted share; computed per scenario and probability-weighted with the IV weights.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate; the 10% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth; base pair 10% / 2.5%. Cap 13x binds at most cells so the grid is flatter across g than across WACC.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a documented repeat of contract-estimation failure (2016 write-back -> 2024 DoJ/SEC settlement -> FY2026 A$125m EBIT loss), a two-customer revenue base (US Navy/USCG + Commonwealth of Australia), and owner FCF negative in four of the last seven periods. Bull trimmed to 30%, read as roughly the probability that a sale of Austal USA completes near the indicative range AND standalone execution is fixed -- it needs several things to go right. Base 45%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band is degenerate: SBC is 0.15% of revenue so street IV exceeds house IV by only ~A$0.12/share; the price sits far outside the band, so band_position is reported as null rather than a meaningless multiple.

takeover_analysis.status: Two competing NON-BINDING indications of interest for Austal USA (Mobile AL yard + San Diego + Singapore support) -- Hanwha Defense USA US$1.05-1.20bn EV (10-Aug-2026, 4-week due diligence granted) and Wildcat Infrastructure US$1.25-1.35bn EV (9-Sep-2026, seeking due diligence). Both cash-free/debt-free. Approvals needed: US (CFIUS/DoD consent for a Navy prime), FIRB conditions on Hanwha's 19.9% stake, Austal board and likely shareholder vote.

sotp_deal_completes.method: Austal USA at bid EV less friction (tax leakage -- Australian participation exemption should shelter most of a share-sale gain but US tax, deal costs and a working-capital/advance-payment adjustment on a cash-free basis are uncertain -- 10-20% haircut) + Australasia standalone DCF (FY2026 revenue A$651m, EBIT A$85.3m; valued at A$450-750m on a 10% mid-cycle EBIT margin doubling revenue by FY2031 at a 13x cap) - capitalised unallocated corporate cost (~A$120m) + group net cash A$182m, over 423.6m diluted shares.

takeover_analysis.deal_probability_rationale: Two bidders and reported DoD support for Hanwha argue up; non-binding status, a foreign acquirer of a US Navy prime, the FY2026 onerous-contract discovery inside diligence, and Austal's own stated strategic value of the US yard argue down. 50% is a coin flip stated as such.
takeover_analysis.deal_adjusted_iv_note: deal_probability x sotp_deal_completes.mid + (1 - deal_probability) x probability_weighted.weighted_iv. This is the figure a reader should act on for the special situation; weighted_iv is the standalone operating value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Standalone, Austal is worth about A$2.55/share probability-weighted (bear A$0.34 / base A$2.22 / bull A$4.89) against a A$4.54 price: the operating business does not support the price. The price is explained instead by the live Austal USA bids -- the sum of the parts under deal-completes is ~A$4.94 (range A$3.99-A$5.94), and a 50% deal probability gives a deal-adjusted A$3.74. At A$4.54 the market is implying roughly a 83% chance of a sale at the mid-range bid. This is a special situation priced as one, not a mispriced compounder.
key_judgments: The FY2026 loss is treated as REAL cash cost spread over FY2027-FY2029 (via the margin path), not as a non-cash one-off to be added back -- provisions on fixed-price contracts are simply losses recognised early.

Mature cash EBITDA of 9.5% (base) sits at the middle of Austal's own FY2019-FY2025 range and below the FY2025 10.2%; the 27% cash tax and 3.75% maintenance capex are why the mature owner-FCF margin (3.3%) is half the FY2019-FY2020 level.
The bull scenario's 18x cap is the only place a strategic-buyer multiple enters the standalone DCF; it is evidenced by the bids, not assumed.

Risk is charged once: in the flows (unwind, capex, thin margins) and in a 25% bear weight -- not in a WACC premium. The sanity check may still want a cap or WACC adjustment for concentration; if so, apply it there and not on top of the bear weight.
what_would_change_the_view: A BINDING agreement for Austal USA at or above US$1.2bn EV with regulatory path clarified -> move deal_probability to 80%+ and the deal-adjusted IV toward the SOTP mid/high (A$4.9-5.9).
Both proposals lapse -> the stock re-rates to the standalone weighted IV; bear weight would rise further.
FY2027 H1 results showing USA Shipbuilding EBIT positive with no further provision movement -> lift base underlying margin toward 10% and cut the unwind assumption.
The FY2026 annual report entering the pipeline -> refresh borrowings, the provision balance (cash-unwind size), diluted shares and segment EBITDA.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
